t: You're standing at Pelham Crescent, a Georgian crescent of houses in South Kensington, dating from around 1825. It was designed by the architect George Basevi, a pupil of Sir John Soane, who also designed Belgrave Square and the Fitzwilliam Museum in Cambridge. Basevi was surveyor to the Thurloe estate, which fits his work in this area. The houses are listed Grade II*, in two groups, numbers one to fourteen and fifteen to twenty-seven. Sir John Hogg, who lived here, is among its residents.
